voyage.name: Orquesta Nacional de España
voyage.content: Tickets are sold at ticket offices in the Auditorio Nacional de Música, Teatro María Guerrero, Teatro de la Zarzuela, Teatro de la Comedia, and Teatro Valle-Inclán.

voyage.name: Orquesta de la Comunidad de Madrid
Banda Sinfónica Municipal de Madrid
voyage.content: Performs in El Retiro Park in the summer. Tickets can be purchased at the Teatro Monumental (listed above), at the tourist information centre in Plaza Mayor, and online.

voyage.name: La Trashumancia
voyage.content: Annual event during which the centre of Madrid is free of cars and is instead filled with shepherds exercising their ancient right to drive sheep and livestock through the city.

voyage.name: Madrid Gay Pride
voyage.content: Annual event held between the last week of June and the first of July, with more than 1.5 million people in the street from all around the world. It began as a weekend party, but lately turned into a full-week extravaganza.

voyage.name: Sol area
voyage.content: The most convenient area for tourists is around Calle de Preciados and Calle del Carmen, between metro stations Sol and Gran Vía, home to the El Corte Inglés department store, high-street names like Zara, Gran Vía 32, H&M, Sephora, Pimkie.

voyage.name: Salamanca
voyage.content: The most upscale shopping district is northeast of the centre, around Calle Serrano and its side-streets. Top designer names like Chanel, Versace, Hermès, Hugo Boss, Louis Vuitton, Emporio Armani and Dolce & Gabbana, including the fluid fabrics and elegant cuts of Spanish designer Adolfo Domínguez, are on Calle Ortega y Gasset. Head for Calle Serrano for Purificación García, Roberto Verino, Ermenegildo Zegna, Loewe,

voyage.name: Chueca and Calle Fuencarral area
voyage.content: This part of the city used to be an abandoned and marginal area. However, it has quickly turned into the most avant-garde and modern part of Madrid. Thanks to the gay community, old shops were taken over and turned into the coolest places of Madrid. Today it is an example of modernity, a paradise for entertainment where everything is possible. The streets are filled with restaurants, alternative cafés and shops, a go

voyage.name: El Corte Inglés Preciados
voyage.content: Occupying the full first few blocks of the pedestrian boulevard Calle Preciados, El Corte Inglés serves as a gateway to the shopping paradise from Puerta de Sol.

voyage.name: El Corte Inglés Plaza de Callao
voyage.content: A much smaller store is to be found at the other end of Calle Preciados. Not quite a looker from the outside, it holds a top-floor restaurant with brilliant views over the Gran Vía.

voyage.name: Calle Cava Baja
voyage.content: This narrow street in La Latina is by far the most famous and popular place for tapas.

voyage.name: Plaza de Cibeles
voyage.content: A massive roundabout at the intersection of Calle de Alcala and Paseo del Prado, this plaza houses one of Madrid's emblems, the Fountain of Cibeles, which portrays the Roman goddess of fertility sitting upon a chariot pulled by two lions. On the southeast corner dominating the Plaza is one of the world's most beautiful city halls, the Palacio de Cibeles (formerly the Palacio de las Comunicaciones), an impressive stru

voyage.name: Museo del Prado
voyage.price: €15 (adults), €7.50 (seniors 65+), free (children/students under 25); free admission within 2 hours of closure; additional obligatory fee for special exhibits
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat 10:00-20:00, Sun 10:00-19:00; closed/shortened hrs on some holidays; extended hrs for special exhibits; last admission 30 min before closing
voyage.content: One of the finest art collections in the world and the best collection of classical art in Madrid. It includes many different collections: the Spanish (El Greco, Velázquez, and Goya), the Flemish and Dutch (Rubens, van Dyck, and Brueghel), Italian (Botticelli, Tintoretto, Titian, Caravaggio, and Veronese) and German (Albrecht Dürer, Lucas Cranach, and Baldung Grien).Some highlights not to miss at the Prado include th

voyage.name: Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía
voyage.alt: Museo Reina Sofía / Reina Sofía National Museum and Art Center
voyage.content: Housed in a former public hospital with an adjacent modern wing, this museum contains Spain's largest collection of 20th century art. Created to house Pablo Picasso's renowned Guernica, allowed after the return of democracy to Spain, the work was initially behind armoured glass. That's gone, but you are kept further away from it that anywhere else in the gallery, and another room includes some Picasso etchings that w

voyage.name: Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza
voyage.price: €13 (adults), €9 (concessions), free (children under 12) and all at certain times (see website)
voyage.hours: Permanent collection and Francisco Bores: Tue-Sun 10:00-19:00, Mon 12:00-16:00; Bulgari and Rome collections: Tue-Fri 10:00-19:00, Sat 10:00-21:00, Sun 10:00-19:00
voyage.content: Contains a large art collection including masterpieces by Monet, Goya, Degas, Renoir, Van Gogh, Picasso, Mondrian, Bacon and Lichtenstein.

voyage.name: CaixaForum Madrid
voyage.price: €6, free (La Caixa account holders), free on 15 May, 18 May, 9 Nov
voyage.content: A private centre particularly well-known for the 'vertical garden' by Patrick Blanc installed on a wall in front of the museum, as well as the quite special architecture of the building itself. The vertical garden can be seen from the street outside, just a block south of the Thyssen-Bornemisza and across from the Prado. The museum only displays temporary exhibitions, usually of a very high quality, in fields ranging

voyage.name: Museo Naval de Madrid
voyage.content: A beautiful museum with a large interesting collection about Spanish naval history, from the efforts of kingdoms of Aragon and Castilia, the many successes and few failures (what's known in English as the defeat of the Spanish Armarda has a section) in the 15th-17th centuries, the drastic decline in the 19th century and its consequences in terms of losing the country's empire, the division of the navy into opposing s

voyage.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
voyage.price: €3 (adults), €1.50 (concessions), free (seniors/students/children under 18); free Sa after 14:00 and Su
voyage.content: Small but interesting museum with artefacts and models from the indigenous people of Asia (mainly the Philippines, former colony of Spain), Africa and America. The exhibits are described in Spanish; however, on each floor, there is a leaflet in English explaining all sections.

voyage.name: Parque del Retiro
voyage.content: The main park of Madrid, the perfect place to take a rest during a sunny day, or take part in the drum circles around the statue of Alphonso XII on summer evenings. There is a large boating lake where one can hire a rowing boat - great fun for the children! There is a monument to the victims of the Madrid 3/11 terrorist bombings, the Forest of the Absent, and the Crystal Palace, a large structure entirely made of gla

voyage.name: Real Jardín Botánico de Madrid
voyage.hours: Nov-Feb: daily 10:00-18:00; Mar/Oct: daily 10:00-19:00; Apr/Sep: daily 10:00-20:00; May-Aug: daily 10:00-21:00
voyage.address: Pl. Murillo, 2, Retiro. Close to Museo Nacional del Prado.
voyage.content: Established in 1755, the garden has been in its current location since 1774. Its extensive collection is dispersed over seven sections, five greenhouses, and a herbarium. A map of the garden is available here.

voyage.name: Banda Sinfónica Municipal de Madrid
voyage.content: An orchestra that performs in El Retiro Park in the summer. Tickets can be purchased at the Teatro Monumental (listed above) and at the tourist information centre in Plaza Mayor, as well as online.

voyage.name: Cuesta de Moyano
voyage.content: A quaint outdoor book market.

voyage.name: Museo del Jamón
voyage.content: Tapas restaurant

voyage.name: 100 Montaditos
voyage.content: Tapas restaurant

voyage.name: Las Adelitas Restaurante Mexicano
voyage.content: Mid-range Mexican restaurant with an extensive range of authentic options, though do be aware the food portions are a lot larger than you would typically expect. The primary chef is from Oaxaca.

voyage.name: FoggBar Birras & Burgers
voyage.content: You can have 2 litres of sangría in a self service dispenser from just €14, or €13 for 2 litres of beer, and you get a free plate of patatas bravas. They also have a delicious selection of bocatas from €2.45. Big TV to watch the football matches while enjoying eating and drinking. If you say you've read this, they'll invite you to a glass of rosado wine.

voyage.name: Kapital
voyage.content: Enormous club with 7 floors. However, despite its popularity this club is usually not worth visiting. The owner has a policy to try to limit the number of foreigners in the club so if you are from anywhere except Spain, you will likely get bad treatment.

voyage.name: Petit Palace Lealtad Plaza
voyage.content: Stylish 4 star-hotel in the Retiro district in central Madrid.

voyage.name: Museo Lázaro Galdiano
voyage.price: €6 (adults), €3 (seniors/students/disabled), free (children under 12); free admission Tu-Sa 15:30-16:30 and Su 14:00-15:00
voyage.hours: Tue-Sat 10:00-16:30, Sun 10:00-15:00; closed Jan 1, Easter Thu and Fri, May 2 and 3, Nov 1, Dec 6 and 25
voyage.content: This museum houses the stunning collection of Spanish entrepreneur José Lázaro Galdiano (1862-1947) and is considered to be one of the best private collections in Spain. Not only will you find works by Goya, Velázquez, El Greco and others - the museum is also filled with jewelry, furniture, sculpture and ceramics. It is located in Lázaro Galdiano's rather lavish former residence. This is an excellent museum that is u

voyage.name: Museo Arqueológico Nacional
voyage.price: €3 (adults), €1.50 (concessions); free on Sa after 14:30, Su mornings, and national holidays
voyage.content: Don't let the sound of it frighten you. This large, well-designed museum opened again in April 2014 after several years of renovation works. It houses an incredible collection of archaeological finds from across the peninsula. It leaves the visitor with a sense of the chronology of civilization in Spain (Iberian, Phoenician, Greek, Roman, Visigoth, Arab, and into the modern age). The famous Dama de Elche, an Iberian

voyage.name: Fundación Juan March
voyage.content: A few blocks off high-end shopping street Calle Serrano, this private foundation houses free temporary exhibitions of (mostly 20th-century) art which are often worth checking out. 10-15 min walk from either Museo Lázaro Galdiano or National Archaeology Museum.

voyage.name: Parque de El Capricho
voyage.hours: Oct-Mar: Sat Sun and holidays 09:00-18:30 (last admission at 18:00); Apr-Sep: Sat Sun and holidays 09:00-21:00 (last admission at 20:30)
voyage.content: One of the most beautiful parks in Madrid. Built in 1797-1839, it has a strong Romanticism influence. Declared as an Historic Garden, its lakes with swans and ducks, labyrinths, palaces, squares and fountains makes this a lovely place.

voyage.name: Plaza de Toros de Las Ventas
voyage.content: Arguably the most important bullfighting site in Spain. Unless you find this spectacle distasteful, this is a must see if you visit Madrid during the bullfighting season (May, during San Isidro). Tickets may nevertheless be expensive and hard to get for the more important corridas. Anyway, it usually is used as a venue for shows and concerts.

voyage.name: El Corte Inglés Centro Comercial Serrano
El Corte Inglés Centro Comercial Goya
Adolfo Domínguez
voyage.content: Flagship store of the Spanish fashion designer. Another branch is in Calle Serrano 96.

voyage.name: Casa Loewe Madrid
voyage.content: Flagship store of one of the world's oldest luxury fashion brands, founded back in the middle of the 19th century in Madrid.

voyage.name: Loewe Flores
voyage.content: Another branch, just around the corner.

voyage.name: Joyería Suarez
voyage.content: Jewellery

voyage.name: Christian Dior
voyage.address: Calle de José Ortega y Gasset, 6

voyage.name: Tiffany & Co.
voyage.address: Calle de José Ortega y Gasset, 10
voyage.content: Exclusive silver jewellery

voyage.name: Hermès
voyage.address: Calle de José Ortega y Gasset, 12

voyage.name: Dolce&Gabbana
voyage.address: Calle de José Ortega y Gasset, 14

voyage.name: Chanel
voyage.address: Calle de José Ortega y Gasset, 16

voyage.name: La Casa del Abuelo 3
voyage.content: A third branch of the popular establishment.

voyage.name: Estay Restaurante
voyage.content: A great place for tapas, they offer a large menu, reasonable prices and excellent quality food. The solomillo al foie is excellent and the desserts come highly-recommended as well. Very crowded on Friday and Saturday nights.

voyage.name: Bar Jaén III
voyage.content: An excellent tapas bar and restaurant. A nice place to enjoy Spanish food and lifestyle without spending too much. Located in a business park in the far-east of the city, it's far from being a tourist trap and you can enjoy good food and true raciónes (portions). The pleasant owners are very willing to share stories about Madrid and Spain more generally. In summer time it has a superb terrace, within a stone's throw

voyage.name: La Trainera
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat 13:00-16:00 20:00-24:00; closed the month of Aug
voyage.content: A Madrid institution for decades, Trainera is an excellent but somewhat pricey restaurant serving strictly seafood dishes. They have a great wine selection and the waiters can recommend different vintages that will complement the food. Try the carabineros (giant scarlet shrimp) or the rodaballo (turbot).

voyage.name: Osuna
voyage.content: A bit outlying, some 20 minutes metro ride to the central districts.

voyage.name: Gran Hotel Velazquez
voyage.content: The Gran Hotel Velázquez is a 4 star hotel located in the Salamanca district. This hotel has been providing stylish accommodation for over 50 years.

voyage.name: Gran Meliá Fénix
voyage.content: Distinguished by a grand and glowing white exterior; bathed in neo-classical design; an illustrious interior of flowing banisters, bold colors, and noble décor.

voyage.name: Hotel Villa Magna
voyage.content: A 5-star hotel on one of Madrid's most exclusive streets. 151 rooms and suites. The hotel is surrounded by landscaped gardens.

voyage.name: Torres de Colón
voyage.content: Eye-catching twin towers, constructed 1967–74. With 116 metres and height and 23 floors, they are among the highest buildings in Madrid.

voyage.name: Plaza de Olavide
voyage.content: Circular place and nice green space (thanks to the motorised traffic being directed through a tunnel), surrounded by an ensemble of colourful 19th-century residential buildings.

voyage.name: Nuevos Ministerios
voyage.content: The modern government complex had already been planned by the republican government before the Civil War, but it was only completed in 1942 under the Francoist rule. Its architectural style is Neoclassical. The ministries of public works and labour are seated here.

voyage.name: Hospital de Maudes
voyage.content: Former hospital complex, built in 1916 in an eclecticist style (similar to Palacio de Cibeles, that was designed by the same architects). It includes a church, Santa María del Silencio. The hospital was intended to serve the poorer classes, therefore nicknamed Hospital de Jornaleros ("hospital of day labourers"). After the Civil War it became a military hospital, before falling out of use in 1970. In the 1980s, it wa

voyage.name: Constitutional Tribunal
voyage.content: Modern circular building from the early 1980s, designed by architects Bonet and Valdés.

voyage.name: Plaza de Castilla
voyage.content: On the north side of the city and bisected by Paseo de la Castellana, this plaza is in the center of Madrid's skyscraper district. A tall obelisk sits in the center of the plaza while the Gate of Europe (Puerta de Europa) towers, two slanted towers which frame the boulevard, are on the north side of the plaza. Taking the #27 bus, which runs along Paseo del Prado and Paseo de la Castellana and ends at Plaza de Castill

voyage.name: Cuatro Torres
voyage.content: Four sleek skyscrapers, constructed between 2004 and 2009. Standing 224 to 249 metres tall, they are the highest in Spain. From south to north, they are named Torre Cepsa, Torre PwC, Torre de Cristal, and Torre Espacio. In the latter, the embassies of Great Britain, Australia and Canada are seated.

voyage.name: Monumento a Rizal
voyage.content: Honors Filipino national hero José Rizal (1861-1896), a revolutionary who was executed by the Spanish in Manila. This is a replica of the more famous "Motto Stella", which is located near his execution site at Rizal Park. This replica was built and inaugurated in 1996, marking the 100 year anniversary of Rizal's death. In the decades since its inauguration, it's become an important landmark for Filipinos visiting Mad

voyage.name: Basílica La Milagrosa
voyage.content: Church from the 1900s in Neo-Mudéjar and Gothic revival style, dedicated to Our Lady of Miracles.

voyage.name: Museo Sorolla
voyage.price: €3 (adults), €1.50 (concessions); free admission Sa after 14:00 and all day Su
voyage.content: This museum is in what was the impressionist painter's house and features fine furniture and porcelain as well as his paintings.

voyage.name: Estación de Chamberí
voyage.price: Free, booking from website (Spanish) linked from English site.
voyage.content: Former metro station designed by architect Antonio Palacios (creator of the Palacio de Cibeles, Círculo de Bellas Artes and Hospital de Maudes). It was inaugurated in 1919, but closed in 1966, thereby becoming a "ghost station". Since 2008 it has been converted to a museum, exhibiting original counters, signs, maps and advertising posters from earlier ages.

voyage.name: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales
voyage.alt: MCNM / National Museum of Natural Sciences
voyage.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat Sun and holidays 10:00-20:00; Sat Sun in Aug 10:00-15:00
voyage.content: Contains a large collection of fossils and minerals, plus educational exhibits (some are described in English but many are in Spanish only). Has two parts open to visitors with separate entrances. The ticket is purchased at the main entrance and to visit the other part you need to exit from the main entrance, turn left and follow the building until you reach the second entrance. Your ticket will be checked again ther

voyage.name: Museo Geominero
voyage.content: Part of the Spanish Institute of Geology and Mining, this museum is dedicated to Geology (with a focus on Mineralogy) and Paleontology, containing an impressive collection of fossils and minerals discovered on the territory of Spain and abroad. Also contains educational exhibits, although all are described in Spanish only. The interior of the building is just as impressive and may be worth a quick tour even if you ar

voyage.name: Museo Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnología
voyage.alt: MUNCYT / National Museum of Science and Technology
voyage.content: The main entry for this museum has been moved to Alcobendas

voyage.name: Auditorio Nacional de Música
voyage.hours: Ticket office: Mon 16:00-18:00, Tue-Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat 11:00-13:00; closed Sat in July and the month of Aug
voyage.content: The main concert venue for the Spanish National Orchestra and the Madrid Symphony Orchestra, as well as the main venue for touring classical artists and orchestras.

voyage.name: Orquesta Nacional de España
voyage.content: Tickets are sold at ticket offices in the Auditorio Nacional de Música, Teatro María Guerrero, Teatro de la Zarzuela, Teatro de la Comedia, and Teatro Valle-Inclán.

voyage.name: Real Madrid
voyage.content: For football fanatics, a trip to the Santiago Bernabeu, the home of local club Real Madrid is not to be missed. Real Madrid is the most successful football club in Spain and Europe, having been crowned Spanish champions a record 32 times and European champions a record 11 times. Their biggest rivals by far are FC Barcelona, with which it contests matches known popularly as El Clásico at least twice a year. The rivalr

voyage.name: Cines Dreams
voyage.content: This cinema is located in a shopping mall known for its ice-skating rink. It is a great place where teenagers can hang out since the mall also has restaurants, bars, and shops.

voyage.name: El Corte Inglés Nuevos Ministerios
voyage.content: If for some reason you will end up in the concrete jungle of Nuevos Ministerios with time to kill, there is an 8-storey sprawling El Corte Inglés for your delight just over the station.

voyage.name: Home Burger Bar
voyage.content: The place for serious hamburgers. Americans will feel at home!

voyage.name: Restaurante Samm
voyage.content: Best paella in Madrid, but only if you bring more than two people by order of the proprietor. Frequented mainly by locals, prepare to be stared at by the wait staff if you are from out of town.

voyage.name: Casa Nemesio
voyage.content: Seafood.

voyage.name: El Telégrafo
voyage.content: Arguably the best seafood in Madrid.

voyage.name: Cervecería Oldenburg
voyage.content: Craft beers & good selection of Belgian & German Beers

voyage.name: Beerhouse Craftbeer Bar
voyage.content: Craft beer bar with a mixture of local & foreign beers.

voyage.name: Cervecería L'Europe
voyage.content: Small beer hall with a small food selection.

voyage.name: Safestay Madrid Central
voyage.content: Hostel with private & shared rooms. chain with hostels in many large European cities.

voyage.name: Caballero Errante
voyage.content: 3 star hotel with modern features, clean rooms and helpful staff. Just over 1.5km walk from the Bernabeu Stadium.

voyage.name: Pension Paquita
voyage.content: Family-run.

voyage.name: Eurostars Suites Mirasierra
voyage.content: A modern luxury hotel located in prestigious residential district Mirasierra, overlooking the Sierra de Guadarama. Facilities include a fitness centre, free parking, and free Wi-Fi. The hotel is also home to the Restaurante Verdil.

voyage.name: Parque Madrid Río
voyage.content: The motorway that used to carve into the city and blight the banks of Río Manzanares, was banished into a tunnel, in a superlative urban landscaping project that cost some €4 billion. Nowadays, a unique 6-km-long landscape garden accompanies the river on both banks. For this project, 33 bridges were dedicated, which allow you to cross from one side to another whenever you want, as well as 5500 benches installed and 3

voyage.name: Planetario de Madrid
voyage.price: Entry is free but the sessions in the planetarium each have a cost of €3.60 for a regular ticket and €1.65 for a reduced ticket (children and seniors)
voyage.content: Features several exhibits related to space exploration, two screens playing documentaries, an interactive area and, of course, the planetarium. Projections last 45 minutes each. Different ones play on different days, so check their website. All the exhibits are explained in Spanish only and the projections in the planetarium are also in Spanish.

voyage.name: Museo de Ferrocarril de Madrid
voyage.price: M-Th F before 14:00, holidays: €6 adult, €4 concession, free child under 4; F after 14:00, Sa Su €2.50
voyage.hours: Oct-May: Mon-Thu 09:30-15:00, Fri and holidays 10:00-18:00, Sat Sun 10:00-20:00; Jun-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-15:00
voyage.content: Museum with four railway tracks, exhibiting a large number of steam, diesel and electric locomotives used in Spain in the 19th and 20th century. Also on display are several model railways. Exhibits are described in Spanish only.

voyage.name: Matadero Madrid
voyage.hours: Usually Tue-Fri 16:00-21:00, Sat Sun 11:00-21:00, on Mon only the cinetheque is opened
voyage.content: Madrid's former main abattoir (matadero), an early 20th-century industrial brick compound in Arganzuela district, has been converted to an arts and cultural centre since the 2000s. It is intended to serve as a cross-disciplinary laboratory of contemporary arts, including studios, exhibition spaces, a theatre, an arthouse cinema, and a library, as well as a café. One of the preferred spots of the city's "artsy" crowd

voyage.name: Sala La Riviera
voyage.address: Paseo Bajo de la Virgen del Puerto, s/n
voyage.content: Another large venue for touring rock and pop bands.

voyage.name: Gruta '77
voyage.content: Concerts everyday: pop, rock, and punk.

voyage.name: Madrid Open
voyage.content: Held in mid-May at La Caja Mágica.

voyage.name: Freiduría de Gallinejas Embajadores
voyage.content: Another classic tapas bar in Madrid, not for conservative stomachs. Their most popular tapas are two of the most typical and traditional dishes in Madrid: gallinejas and entresijos. A treat for adventurous palates and lamb-lovers.

voyage.name: Café Ziryab Tablao Flamenco
voyage.content: A Flamenco venue with daily shows at 21:30 by first line artists, in an intimate ambiance. Kind staff, nice drinks and tapas, personalized attention and the artists right in front of you.

voyage.name: La Esquina de Eusebio
voyage.content: Trays of tapas are passed from one person to another in this typical bar of Madrid, absolutely not touristy but really worth it. And it's not so far from the centre.

voyage.name: Sol Hostel
voyage.content: Rooms from 4 to 14 people, plus breakfast and internet (WIFI).

voyage.name: Faunia
voyage.price: €26.45 (adults), €19.95 (seniors/children), €18.45 (disabled), free (children under 3); ticket prices are significantly cheaper if purchase online
voyage.content: Zoological park. Different sections of the park include animals from different locations (Africa, Antarctica etc..)

voyage.name: Gruta '77
voyage.content: Concerts everyday – pop, rock, and punk.

voyage.name: Kinépolis
voyage.content: Outside the city, in the suburb of Pozuelo de Alarcon. When inaugurated, it was the largest megaplex in the world by number of seats. Has 25 screens. Typically on weekends only the new releases are offered in their original version, however Tuesday is "V.O. Day" when all movies are offered in their original version.

voyage.name: Madrid Open
voyage.content: Held in mid-May at La Caja Mágica.

voyage.name: Rayo Vallecano
voyage.content: Rayo were relegated in 2019 so they now play in Segunda División, the second tier of Spanish football. Their home ground is Campo de Fútbol de Vallecas, capacity 15,000. It's in the Portazgo district, 2 km southeast of Atocha station, take Metro to Portazgo.

voyage.name: Bacchus
voyage.content: Right in the middle of Lonja, an area filled with places to dine and drink. It is still close enough to city centre but offers a more relaxed ambience, making it one especially suitable for families, though all types of customers can be encountered. Bacchus offers a mixture of innovative and traditional-style tapas. Very good though expensive wine list. It can get very busy on weekends. Nice outside seating area make

voyage.name: Aparthotel Encasa
voyage.address: Carr. de Vicálvaro a la Estación de O'donnell 18

voyage.name: Museo Nacional de Ciencias Naturales
voyage.alt: MCNM / National Museum of Natural Sciences
voyage.hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat Sun and holidays 10:00-20:00; Sat Sun in Aug 10:00-15:00
voyage.content: Contains a large collection of fossils and minerals, plus educational exhibits (some are described in English but many are in Spanish only). Has two parts open to visitors with separate entrances. The ticket is purchased at the main entrance and to visit the other part you need to exit from the main entrance, turn left and follow the building until you reach the second entrance. Your ticket will be checked again ther

voyage.name: Plaza de Castilla
voyage.content: On the north side of the city and bisected by Paseo de la Castellana, this plaza is in the center of Madrid's skyscraper district. A tall obelisk sits in the center of the plaza while the Gate of Europe (Puerta de Europa) towers, two slanted towers which frame the boulevard, are situated on the north side of the plaza. Taking the #27 bus, which runs along Paseo del Prado and Paseo de la Castellana and ends at Plaza d

voyage.name: Parque de El Capricho
voyage.hours: Oct-Mar: Sat Sun and holidays 09:00-18:30 (last admission at 18:00); Apr-Sep: Sat Sun and holidays 09:00-21:00 (last admission at 20:30)
voyage.content: One of the most beautiful parks in Madrid. Built in 1797-1839, it has a strong Romanticism influence. Declared as an Historic Garden, its lakes with swans and ducks, labyrinths, palaces, squares and fountains makes this a lovely place.

voyage.name: Spanish National Research Council Headquarters
voyage.content: Headquarters of the largest public institution dedicated to research in Spain and the third largest in Europe. Not a real touristic place, and they would probably not let you in to take a photo of the building, but this is the main filming location of the Royal Mint of Spain in the Spanish Emmy winner TV show, Money Heist (La Casa De Papel).

voyage.name: Palacio Real de El Pardo
voyage.content: It was built as a hunting lodge for the Spanish royal family, and was commandeered by Francisco Franco to serve as his residence. Today it serves as the official guest house for foreign dignitaries visiting Madrid, and is also open to the public when not in use. Check out the vast collection of tapestries hanging from the palace walls, some of which were even designed by the painter Francisco Goya.

voyage.name: Auditorio Nacional de Música
voyage.hours: Ticket office: Mon 16:00-18:00, Tue-Fri 10:00-17:00, Sat 11:00-13:00; closed Sat in July and the month of Aug
voyage.content: The main concert venue for the Spanish National Orchestra and the Madrid Symphony Orchestra, as well as the main venue for touring classical artists and orchestras.

voyage.name: Real Madrid
voyage.content: They play soccer in La Liga, the top tier, and are the most successful football club not only in Spain but in Europe, having been Spanish champions 32 times and European champions 14 times. Their biggest rivals are FC Barcelona, and these twice-yearly El Clásico matches sell out quickly, as does El Derbi against local rivals Atlético de Madrid. Their stadium, the Santiago Bernabéu, has a capacity of 81,000. It's one

voyage.name: Atlético de Madrid
voyage.content: They play in La Liga, the top tier, and are one of the most successful teams in Spain, having won both La Liga and the Copa del Rey on ten occasions. They were European Cup runners-up in 2014 and 2016 and won the UEFA Europa League in 2010 and 2012. Since 2017 their home ground is Estadio Metropolitano, capacity 67,700, also known as Wanda Metropolitano. It's 10 km east of city centre in San Blas district, with its o

voyage.name: El Corte Inglés Castellana
voyage.content: If for some reason you will end up in the concrete jungle of Nuevos Ministerios with time to kill, the flagship 8-storey sprawling El Corte Inglés is there for your delight just beside the station.

voyage.name: Centro Comercial La Vaguada
voyage.content: Mostly patronized by locals, Madrid's first and oldest shopping mall has several stores from Spanish and foreign brands to suit your fancy, as well as several restaurants and a cinema.

voyage.name: Palacio de Hielo
voyage.content: Popular with locals, especially among the residents of surrounding Hortaleza, this mall contains Madrid's only year-round ice skating rink (hence the name), as well as a gym, a bowling alley, a minigolf course and a swimming pool, plus a cinema and several shops and restaurants.

voyage.name: Caleido
voyage.content: Madrid's newest shopping mall, the podium of the Torre Caleido office tower in the Cuatro Torres Business Area is home to exclusive stores, several art installations and a variety of restaurants and bars which close later (until 02:00 the next day) than the mall.

voyage.name: Home Burger Bar
voyage.content: Other burger bars of this brand can be found in Malasaña-Chueca.

voyage.name: Churrería La Andaluza
voyage.content: Opened in the 1930s just beside the Mercado de Maravillas, this Tetuán institution is regarded as one of the best churrerías in Madrid, with freshly-made churros, porras and buñuelos (round, donut-shaped fritters) available year-round.

voyage.name: Bar Tambayan
voyage.content: Located in the northern reaches of Tetuán, this is arguably the best Filipino restaurant in Madrid, located in the heart of the city's Filipino neighborhood.

voyage.name: Pastelería Mifer
voyage.content: This unassuming bakery in Ciudad Lineal sells a wide variety of cakes and pastries, but they are best known for their award-winning torrijas (Spanish-style French toast) sold only during the run-up to Lent.

voyage.name: Cafetería Nebraska
voyage.content: Known throughout Madrid for their hot dogs, this Tetuán diner is the last of an old chain of restaurants dating back to 1955.

voyage.name: Restaurante Bar Rodrigo
voyage.address: Plaza de la Condesa de Gavia, 3
voyage.content: Located behind the Mercado de Maravillas, this hidden gem in Tetuán serves affordable yet high-quality paellas that can compete with some of the best Madrid has to offer. Mostly patronized by locals, reservations are recommended, especially on weekends.

voyage.name: Restaurante Malaysia
voyage.content: Authentic Malaysian food served right in the heart of San Blas, with an extensive menu drawing from the diverse culinary traditions of Malaysia and its neighbors.

voyage.name: Bar Jaén III
voyage.content: An excellent tapas bar and restaurant. A nice place to enjoy Spanish food and lifestyle without spending too much. Being located just outside central Madrid, it's far from being a tourist trap and you can enjoy good food and true raciónes (portions). The pleasant owners are very willing to share stories about Madrid and Spain more generally. In summer time it has a superb terrace, within a stone's throw of the Olympi

voyage.name: Restaurante Samm
voyage.content: A Chamartín institution lauded as having some of the best paellas (if not the best) in Madrid, but only if you bring more than two people by order of the proprietor. Walk-ins turned away from Casa Benigna on the other end of Chamartín are usually sent here. Frequented mainly by locals, prepare to be stared at by the wait staff if you are from out of town.

voyage.name: Casa Nemesio
voyage.content: Seafood.

voyage.name: El Telégrafo
voyage.content: Arguably the best seafood in Madrid.

voyage.name: Restaurante Casa Benigna
voyage.content: Owned by a Spanish-Norwegian family, this unassuming spot in Chamartín is known for serving traditional Spanish cuisine with a Nordic twist. Their paellas, served on custom-made copper pans, are reportedly among the best (if not the best) in Madrid, with prominent politicians, celebrities and businesspeople among their customers. Reservations recommended well in advance. Walk-ins are routinely turned away at the door

voyage.name: Puerta del Sol
voyage.content: This plaza is the heart of Madrid and one of the busiest places in the city - a hub for the local transit system, a favorite meeting spot for locals, a visible area for festivals or political demonstrations, and an opportune location for tour guides, street performers, pickpockets and anyone else looking to take advantage of all the tourists on-hand. In the center of the plaza sits the Statue of King Charles III on h

voyage.name: Gran Vía
voyage.content: Literally 'Great Way' (better translated as 'Broadway'), Gran Vía is one of the busiest avenues in Madrid. Running from Plaza de España to Plaza de Cibeles, it is the location of the cinema district and a number of shopping malls and is lined with large billboards and lights. There's a constant buzz of traffic and life – 03:00-04:00 early morning traffic jams are not unusual.

voyage.name: Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando
voyage.alt: RABASF / Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando
voyage.price: €10 (adults), €5 (seniors/students over 25), free (students/children under 18); free on W and national holidays
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-15:00; open holidays; closed for the month of Aug
voyage.content: Highly impressive art collection with paintings, sculptures, drawings and prints. Several Goya masterpieces.

voyage.name: La Tabacalera
voyage.content: An abandoned tobacco factory turned into a huge Berlin-like alternative art space driven by the diverse locals of Lavapies district. Also free workshops daily. Nice big cheap outdoors terrace.It is hoped that the closure is temporary and that it will return in a reduced form after works, check website for current situation.

voyage.name: Auditorio 400
voyage.content: The main venue for contemporary music, dance, and theatre performance.

voyage.name: Círculo de Bellas Artes
voyage.hours: Exhibits: Tue-Sun 11:00-14:00 17:00-21:00; Azotea: Mon-Fri 09:00-21:00, Sat Sun and holidays 11:00-21:00
voyage.content: A non-profit cultural center located a short walk from Sol, the CBA offers up a wide variety of events and shows including film, music, art displays, dance, theater and more. See the website (in Spanish) for a list of activities. Great panoramic views of the city can be had from the Azotea, located at the top of the building.

voyage.name: Cardamomo Tablao Flamenco
voyage.content: Authentic Flamenco show in the center of Madrid, one of the greatest tablaos flamencos all over Spain, typical Spanish food during the performance.

voyage.name: Teatro de la Zarzuela
voyage.content: The Spanish version of the operetta (zarzuela) is performed here. This is also the main concert venue for the Community of Madrid Orchestra.

voyage.name: Orquesta de la Comunidad de Madrid
Orquesta Sinfónica de RTVE
voyage.content: Performs every Th and F at the Teatro Monumental on Calle Atocha.

voyage.name: Yelmo Cineplex Ideal
voyage.content: Probably the best known V.O. (versión original, or original language) theatre in Madrid, it offers the largest selection of movies and is a short walk from Sol.

voyage.name: Cine Doré
voyage.content: This is a wonderful old Spanish theatre dating from the 1920s. It has three screens and shows mainly art-house and critically acclaimed films in the original language. In the summertime, they screen movies on the roof.

voyage.name: Essential Flamenco
voyage.content: An authentic flamenco show in the heart of Madrid, set in a traditional exposed brick cave of the XIX century. Daily shows at 18:00, 19:30 and 21:00. Free drink included.

voyage.name: El Corte Inglés Preciados
voyage.content: Occupying the full first few blocks of the pedestrian boulevard Calle Preciados, El Corte Inglés serves as a gateway to the shopping paradise from Puerta de Sol.

voyage.name: El Corte Inglés Plaza de Callao
voyage.content: A much smaller store is to be found at the other end of Calle Preciados. Not quite a looker from the outside, it holds a top-floor restaurant with brilliant views over the Gran Vía.

voyage.name: Cervecería 100 Montaditos
voyage.content: Branch of the popular nationwide chain that offers 100 different montaditos (small sandwiches). Great place to go for a cheap drink and bite to eat. Further branches are at Calle de la Montera, 34 (near metro Gran Vía) and Plaza de las Cortes, 3.

voyage.name: Museo del Jamón
voyage.content: One of several branches of this chain. Offers deli takeout service as well as tapas and raciónes at reasonable prices. They offer €1 ham sandwiches and a 'picnic' lunch consisting of a said ham sandwich, fresh fruit and a drink for €2 (Feb 2017). Another branch is at Calle de Atocha, 54 (metro Antón Martín).

voyage.name: Casa Toni
voyage.content: Very solid local option for small dishes/tapas. Recommended are chorizo, pig ears, tortilla with chorizo (omelette with chorizo), morcilla, sepia a la plancha. Casual non pretentious place.

voyage.name: Matador
voyage.content: Fantastic little stop for tapas. A very cozy place with good tapas and they always treat you very well. With a funny decoration.

voyage.name: Takos Al Pastor
voyage.content: Good taqueria. The tacos are amazing. The quesadillas and tortas are also worth it. The queue seems super long, but it moves fast.

voyage.name: Puerto Rico
voyage.content: Small little cantine with excellent and satisfying authentic Spanish food. You have to queue, but it's quite fluid and it's worth it.

voyage.name: Mercado de San Fernando
voyage.content: Lively market that has not been completely swamped by tourism. Wide range of food & drink available. (including Vegan)

voyage.name: Alhambra
voyage.content: This is a good place to drop by on a hot afternoon to enjoy a cold beer and some Andalusian tapas. Sample the sausages and cheeses.

voyage.name: La Casa del Abuelo
voyage.content: A Madrid landmark in operation for over 100 years, this bar attracts a standing room only crowd on the weekends. They mainly serve shrimp-based tapas dishes so if you're not into shellfish it may be advisable to steer clear. Order a plate of their garlic shrimp and accompany with their house wine.

voyage.name: El Inti de Oro
voyage.content: For something different, try this great Peruvian restaurant a short walk from Sol. Be sure to order some of their ceviche and try the Pisco Sour cocktail.

voyage.name: Viva Chapata
voyage.content: All-vegan restaurant that doesn't compromise on flavor, a good place to try vegan versions of Spanish tortilla and croquetas.

voyage.name: Café Central
voyage.content: Café by day, live jazz music at night.

voyage.name: La Mallorquina
voyage.content: Famous for its pastries. Peaceful upstairs room where you can linger undisturbed over your café con leche and napolitana de chocolate (chocolate croissant).

voyage.name: Nuevo Café Barbieri
voyage.content: Slightly scruffy cafe draws an avante garde crowd at night.

voyage.name: La Pecera del Círculo de Bellas Artes
voyage.alt: Café del Círculo de Bellas Artes
voyage.content: A soaring hall on the ground floor of Madrid's art center combines atmosphere, excellent food and good coffee at reasonable prices. A wonderful place for lunch not far from Madrid's shopping or museums.

voyage.name: Museo Chicote
voyage.content: Voted the Best European Bar 2004 by MTV-Campari. Extensive cocktail list. Claims to have served drinks to many famous celebrities, including, Ava Gardner, Frank Sinatra, Lana Turner, Gary Cooper, Orson Wells, Yul Brynner and Ernest Hemingway, Catherine Zeta Jones, Hugh Grant and Tim Robbins. They only serve drinks.

voyage.name: Dubliners
voyage.content: An Irish bar in the centre of Madrid near Puerta del Sol. The bar has televisions and is one of the places where sport can be seen.

voyage.name: Xaloc Bar de Copas
voyage.content: Discopub in the core of Barrio de las Letras. Great place with excellent prices but a good quality. The bar includes nice music, a DJ, and a moderately large dance floor.

voyage.name: Viva Madrid
voyage.address: Calle de Manuel Fernández y González, 7
voyage.content: Opened in 1856, this Madrid institution is known for its old-world charm and its creative takes on tapas and cocktails. José Rizal, the Philippines' national hero, was a regular patron, with a plaque hanging above the door in his honor.

voyage.name: Chinaski Lavapiés
voyage.content: Interesting mixture of unusual local and foreign beers.

voyage.name: El Sol
voyage.content: Popular with the 20-30 age group. Plays a mix of 70s, funk, and bossanova sounds. No dress code, but people do tend to look cool.

voyage.name: Ohm
voyage.address: Plaza de Callao, 1 (in Gran Via street)
voyage.content: Popular Commercial House club with a mixed young straight/gay crowd.

voyage.name: Stardust
voyage.content: Powerful Techno/House club popular within the younger crowd.

voyage.name: Mad Hostel
voyage.content: Nice, clean, quiet weekend hostel. 5 minutes from metro, tapas and services. 10-minute walk to Puerto del Sol, museums and Gran Via. Close to southern 'ethnic' areas = good food. Big common room with 4 computer stations, unreliable Wi-Fi and good free breakfast. Secure locker with every bed.

voyage.name: Cat's Hostel
voyage.content: Located in a 17th-century palace, but has a modern interior and is clean and secure. Breakfast and internet is included in the price and there is also a bar. It attracts a young backpackers clientele, but the crowd here is such that you're more likely to find partiers than hitchhikers. Shared dormitories for 4 to 14 people.

voyage.name: Way Hostel Residence
voyage.content: Small hostel, nice ambiance and is catered to young travelers. Nice kitchen, friendly staff, and free internet.

voyage.name: Hostal San Martin
voyage.content: Small, clean guest-house on the 4th floor. Ideally located just meters from Gran Via, with great staff and free WI-fi. All rooms have sink & shower, but most share bathrooms.

voyage.name: Hotel ibis Styles Madrid Prado
voyage.content: The small and inconspicuous ibis Styles gets great reviews thanks to a combination of nice rooms, good staff and ideal location, all that at a reasonable price including breakfast.

voyage.name: Hostal Plaza d'Ort
voyage.content: Cheap hotel with a good location near Plaza de Santa Ana. All rooms feature bathrooms, TV and air conditioning.

voyage.name: ibis budget Madrid Centro Lavapies
voyage.content: Budget hotel convenient for metro station. Some single rooms.

voyage.name: Artistic Bed & Breakfast
voyage.content: In the center of Madrid, a quiet bed and breakfast with a unique style and decoration.

voyage.name: Asturias
voyage.content: A 2-star hotel. The Asturias is 200 meters from the central Puerta del Sol.

voyage.name: Hotel Madrid Preciados
voyage.content: 4-star hotel in excellent location.

voyage.name: Hotel Senator Gran Via Madrid
voyage.content: 4-star hotel. Restaurant, bar, and meeting space.

voyage.name: ME Madrid Reina Victoria
voyage.content: Located in Plaza de Santa Ana.

voyage.name: Hotel De Las Letras
voyage.content: Old building with tasteful modern interior. Well sound-proofed against the busy Gran Via outside. Very comfortable beds. Rooms with TV, hi-fi, mini bar, bath/shower. Optional breakfast buffet with wide choice of good quality food and drinks. Pleasant, comfortable bar.

voyage.name: Maria Elena Palace
voyage.content: The Hotel María Elena Palace is located just 200 metres away from the Puerta del Sol. Renowned for its magnificent glass dome in the lobby.

voyage.name: Hotel Quatro Puerta del Sol
voyage.content: The turn-of-the-century grandeur with modern conveniences and amenities. Hotel Quo Puerta del Sol is housed in an emblematic building from the beginning of the 20th century with unique views of the city. It was totally restored in 2003.
